products.name: Nutmeg
products.desc: Whole nutmeg kernels, ready to grate fresh.
products.long: Whole nutmeg kernels with their warm, sweet aroma locked inside. Grate a little fresh over curries, biryanis, custards, cakes and warm milk — whole nutmeg keeps its fragrance far longer than pre-ground spice.
products.usage:
Grate fresh with a fine grater just before use.
A few scrapes go a long way — start with a pinch.
Works in garam masala, biryani, white sauce, baked goods and warm drinks.
products.storage: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight. Always use a dry spoon.

products.name: Mace
products.desc: Aromatic blades of mace — the lacy cover of the nutmeg seed.
products.long: Mace is the bright, lacy covering that wraps the nutmeg seed, dried into fragrant blades. It tastes like a lighter, more delicate nutmeg with a hint of pepper and citrus. Use it whole in biryani, pulao, stocks and pickles, or grind it into spice blends.
products.usage:
Add 1–2 blades whole to rice, biryani or stock; remove before serving.
Dry-roast lightly and grind into garam masala and rubs.
Pairs well with cardamom, cinnamon and clove.
products.storage: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight. Always use a dry spoon.

articles.title: Nutmeg and Mace: Two Spices From One Fruit
articles.excerpt: They grow together inside the same fruit, but nutmeg and mace taste — and cook — differently. Here is how to use each.
articles.author: Skyrah Impex Team
articles.body:
Nutmeg and mace come from the same fruit of the nutmeg tree. Split the fruit open and you find a dark, hard seed wrapped in a bright, lacy covering. The seed becomes nutmeg; the lacy covering, dried into blades, becomes mace.

## How they taste
Nutmeg is warm, sweet and woody. Mace is lighter and more delicate, with a peppery, almost citrus edge. Because mace is gentler, it suits dishes where you want fragrance without heaviness — clear soups, rice and light sauces.

## Whole or ground?
Whole nutmeg holds its aroma for a long time; grate it fresh just before use. Ground nutmeg is convenient for baking, chai and quick sauces. Mace blades can go whole into biryani or stock and be lifted out before serving, or be dry-roasted and ground into spice blends.

## Easy ways to use them
- A pinch of nutmeg in white sauce, mashed potatoes or warm milk.
- Two blades of mace in a pot of pulao or biryani.
- Both together in a homemade garam masala.

> A little goes a long way — start with a pinch and build up.

articles.title: Five Easy Ways to Use Moringa Powder
articles.excerpt: Moringa powder fits into food you already make. Here are five simple ways to add a spoonful to your day.
articles.author: Skyrah Impex Team
articles.body:
Moringa leaves have been part of South Indian cooking for generations — in poriyal, adai and soups. Moringa powder gives you the same leaves in a form that keeps in the pantry and mixes into almost anything.

## 1. Stir it into a smoothie
Add half a teaspoon to a banana or mango smoothie. The fruit balances moringa's earthy taste.

## 2. Finish a bowl of dal or soup
Stir a spoonful into dal, rasam or vegetable soup after you take it off the heat.

## 3. Knead it into dough
Mix a teaspoon into chapati, paratha or adai batter for a green colour and a mild herbal note.

## 4. Blend it into chutney
Add it to coconut or mint chutney while grinding.

## 5. Sprinkle it on snacks
Mix with salt and chilli and dust over roasted makhana, peanuts or popcorn.

> Start small — half a teaspoon is plenty while you get used to the flavour.

articles.title: How to Brew the Perfect Hibiscus Infusion
articles.excerpt: Hot or iced, sweet or tart — a simple guide to a ruby-red cup of hibiscus.
articles.author: Skyrah Impex Team
articles.body:
Hibiscus brews into a striking ruby-red drink with a tart, cranberry-like taste. It is easy to make, and just as good chilled as it is hot.

## The basic hot cup
Use about one teaspoon per cup. Pour hot (just off the boil) water over it and steep for about five minutes. Strain if you like, and sweeten with honey or jaggery to taste.

## Iced hibiscus
Brew at double strength, let it cool, then pour over plenty of ice. Add a squeeze of lime and a few mint leaves.

## Make it your own
- A slice of ginger or a stick of cinnamon while steeping adds warmth.
- A splash of orange juice softens the tartness.
- A pinch of our Spice Tea blend turns it into a spiced winter drink.

> Longer steeping makes a stronger, more tart cup — adjust the time to your taste.

articles.title: Cooking With Dehydrated Vegetables and Powders
articles.excerpt: Okra, onion, garlic and tomato that keep for months — and how to cook with them on a busy day.
articles.author: Skyrah Impex Team
articles.body:
Dehydrating removes the water from vegetables and leaves the flavour behind. The result keeps far longer than fresh produce and is ready whenever you are.

## Dehydrated okra
Soak the rounds in warm water for 10–15 minutes, drain, and cook them as you would fresh okra — in sambar, curry or a quick stir-fry. Or skip the soaking and roast them with oil and spices for a crunchy snack.

## Onion and garlic powders
About one tablespoon of onion powder stands in for a medium onion, and a quarter teaspoon of garlic powder for a clove. They are ideal for marinades, dry rubs, dips and gravies that need to come together fast.

## Tomato powder
Mix a tablespoon with a little water for an instant paste, or stir it straight into rice, soups and curries for colour and tang.

> Keep every pack tightly sealed after opening — moisture is the only thing that spoils a good dried vegetable.

articles.title: From Indian Soil to Global Soul
articles.excerpt: What Skyrah Impex does, and the promise behind every pack we send out.
articles.author: Skyrah Impex Team
articles.body:
Skyrah Impex Private Limited is an import and export company based in Pollachi, Tamil Nadu. We bring the natural produce of India — whole spices, spice powders, dehydrated vegetables, fruit powders and herbal infusions — to kitchens at home and abroad.

## What we stand for
Our line is simple: from Indian soil to global soul. Every product starts with an Indian farm and ends in someone's kitchen, wherever in the world that may be.

## Retail and bulk
You can order individual packs on WhatsApp straight from our shop. For wholesale, private-label or export requirements, send us an enquiry with the product, quantity and destination and we will come back with a quote.

> Questions about a product or an order? Our team is a message away.

faqs.q: How do I place an order?
faqs.a: Open any product and tap "Order on WhatsApp" — the message is filled in with the product and quantity for you. You can also send an enquiry from our Contact page, or call us on the numbers listed there.

faqs.q: Do you take bulk, wholesale and export orders?
faqs.a: Yes. Skyrah Impex is an import and export company. Send us the product, quantity, packing and destination through the Contact page or by email, and we will reply with a quote.

faqs.q: Why do some products say "Ask us" instead of a price?
faqs.a: Prices depend on the pack size and quantity you need. Message us on WhatsApp and we will share the current price.
Orders are packed and dispatched from Pollachi, Tamil Nadu. We deliver across India, and export shipments are arranged on agreed terms.
Most orders within India arrive in 3–6 business days from dispatch. Export timelines depend on the destination and shipping mode, and are confirmed with your quote.

faqs.q: How should I store the products?
faqs.a: Keep every pack tightly sealed in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight, and always use a dry spoon.
The best-before date is printed on every pack. Stored as directed, our dried products keep their quality for months.

faqs.q: Is the Sugar Balance Infusion a medicine?
faqs.a: No. It is a herbal infusion to be enjoyed as a beverage. It is not intended to diagnose, treat or cure any condition — please follow your doctor's advice for any health concern.
Unopened products can be returned within 7 days of delivery. Because these are food items, opened packs can only be returned if there is a quality issue — see our Return & Refund Policy for details.

faqs.q: My order arrived damaged — what do I do?
faqs.a: Message us on WhatsApp or email us within 48 hours of delivery with a photo of the item, and we will arrange a replacement or refund.
Approved refunds are processed within 5–7 business days to your original payment method.
